title: L4 vs L7 Load Balancers & TLS

scenes.line1: Can both L4 and L7 handle TLS?
scenes.say: Can both layer four and layer seven load balancers handle encrypted traffic? Let's break down what really sets them apart.

scenes.label: L4
scenes.sub: Routes by IP and port. Fast, protocol-agnostic.
scenes.say: Layer four routes based on IP address and port. It's fast and works for any protocol, not just web traffic.

scenes.label: L7
scenes.sub: Understands HTTP. Can route by host, path, or headers.
scenes.say: Layer seven actually understands HTTP. It can route by host name, path, or even rewrite headers.

left.title: L4
items: Can terminate TLS in some cases

scenes.say: Both layers can terminate encrypted connections in some setups. But only layer seven can look inside the HTTP and change requests if needed.

scenes.question: Who can terminate TLS connections?
scenes.wrong: Only L7 load balancers can do it.
scenes.right: Both L4 and L7 can terminate TLS, but only L7 can inspect HTTP traffic.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: it's not just layer seven that can end encrypted sessions. Layer four can do it too, but it can't read or change the web traffic inside.
